keyQuotes: Any requirement, once it enters development, must go through at least six stages: 'evidence, hypothesis, scope, schedule, acceptance, and review'.
Adding a new requirement is not 'doing a little more', but a reallocation of resources.

mainPoints.explanation: Mapping the 8 Skills to the four stages of problem assessment, requirement definition, sprint execution, and post-launch review forms a reusable, lightweight working protocol.
mainPoints.point: When an OPC team lacks dedicated product roles, Anthropic PM Skills can carry product judgment and workflow.

mainPoints.explanation: Using synthesize-research and metrics-review to determine if a problem is worth solving avoids wasting resources on the wrong requirements.
mainPoints.point: Before entering requirement definition, problem assessment must be done first rather than directly writing a PRD.

mainPoints.explanation: Indiscriminately feeding materials to AI reduces output confidence; formatted input is a prerequisite for ensuring analysis quality.
mainPoints.point: Before materials enter a Skill, they must be formatted according to five fields: source, time, subject, content, and association.

mainPoints.explanation: 100% capacity planning leaves the team unable to handle uncertainty; reasonable buffering ensures sustainable delivery.
mainPoints.point: Iteration plans should only allocate 70%-80% capacity, reserving a buffer for online issues and ad-hoc collaboration.

oneSentenceSummary: Drawing on Anthropic's Product Management Skills, the JD Health OPC team breaks down the full product cycle into four stages: problem assessment, requirement definition, sprint execution, and post-launch review, providing reusable prompt templates and material input specifications.
originalTitle: 京东健康 OPC 团队的产品全流程 Skill 探索
summary: The article details how the JD Health OPC (One Person Company) team adapted Anthropic's open-source 8 Product Management Skills (synthesize-research, metrics-review, competitive-brief, product-brainstorming, write-spec, roadmap-update, sprint-planning, stakeholder-update) to enhance their product workflow. The author notes that in an OPC team without dedicated product roles, this set of Skills provides a "shared product-engineering decision-making framework" that standardizes the process from requirement emergence to launch. The article unfolds across four stages: the first stage uses synthesize-research and metrics-review to determine if a problem is worth solving; the second stage uses product-brainstorming to diverge on solutions and write-spec to converge on requirement specifications; the third stage uses roadmap-update to determine priorities and sprint-planning to implement the iteration plan; the fourth stage uses metrics-review to review metrics and stakeholder-update to sync with different audiences. The article also provides a 5-field format for material input, prompt templates for each stage, a roadmap change description template, common pitfalls, and a minimal starting path.
title: JD Health OPC Team's Exploration of Full-Cycle Product Skills
